questions.question: Which group has the same amount as one toonie?
questions.explain: A toonie is 2 dollars, which is the same as 2 loonies. More coins does not mean more money; 4 dimes is only 40 cents.

questions.question: Aya has 5 loonies. Her brother has 2 toonies and 1 loonie. Who has more money?
questions.explain: 5 loonies is $5, and 2 toonies plus 1 loonie is $4+$1=$5. They are the same! More coins does not always mean more money.

questions.question: At the market, a bag of apples costs 3 dollars and 25 cents. Priya paid with 3 loonies and 1 quarter. Is that the right amount?
questions.explain: 3 loonies and 1 quarter is 3 dollars and 25 cents, exactly the cost. Don't add 3 and 25 to get 28; dollars and cents are different units.

questions.question: A poster costs 5 dollars and 50 cents. Nina paid with 5 loonies and 5 dimes. Is that the right amount?
questions.explain: 5 loonies and 5 dimes is 5 dollars and 50 cents, which is exactly the cost. Don't read the 5 and the 50 as the single number 55.

questions.question: Zoe has 6 quarters. Her mom has 2 loonies. Who has more money?
questions.explain: 6 quarters is 1 dollar and 50 cents, and 2 loonies is 2 dollars. Mom has more even though she has fewer coins. It is the value that counts.

questions.question: Ben wants to show 2 dollars and 50 cents using only dimes. How many dimes does he need?
questions.explain: 2 dollars and 50 cents is 250 cents. Each dime is 10 cents, so 25 dimes is 250 cents. Don't add 2 and 50 to get 52; they are different units.

questions.question: A book costs $6. Sam paid with 3 toonies. His sister paid with 6 loonies. Did they both pay the same amount?
questions.explain: 3 toonies is $6, and 6 loonies is also $6. Both paid the same amount. Fewer coins can be worth the same as more coins.

questions.question: Lily says 2 loonies and 50 cents equals 52 dimes. What went wrong?
options: She mixed up dimes and nickels
She used dimes instead of loonies
She counted one coin too many
questions.explain: 2 loonies and 50 cents is 2 dollars and 50 cents, which is 25 dimes. The mistake was adding 2 and 50 as if they were the same kind of number.

questions.question: Noa paid 7 loonies and 5 dimes for a ticket. Her friend says she paid $75. Is the friend right?
options: No, it is 7 dollars and 50 cents
No, it is 7 dollars and 5 cents
questions.explain: 7 loonies and 5 dimes is 7 dollars and 50 cents, not 75 dollars. You cannot read the 7 and the 5 as the number 75; the 5 dimes are 50 cents.

questions.question: Three of these groups make 1 dollar. Which group does not?
questions.explain: 4 quarters, 10 dimes and 20 nickels each count up to 100 cents, so each one makes 1 dollar. The group of 3 quarters is only 75 cents.

questions.question: Dev has 2 loonies and 4 quarters. Which group is the same amount?
questions.explain: 4 quarters make 1 dollar, so Dev has 2 dollars and 1 more dollar, which is 3 dollars. Do not just add 2 and 4: quarters are cents, not dollars.

questions.question: Omar has 4 toonies. Which group has the same amount?
questions.explain: A toonie is 2 dollars, so 4 toonies make 8 dollars, just like 8 loonies. More coins does not mean more money: 18 dimes is less than 2 dollars.
